scope: Proposition 4.3 (Extension from a prime floor) of the manuscript “Abundance after nonvanishing for compact Kähler fourfolds” (preprints/Abundance-after-nonvanishing-for-compact-Kahler-fourfolds-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 034 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 89b5dd1a939cd7a6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 24. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 4.1, there are a normal compact analytic space Z, a closed embedding W ,→ Z, and a proper bimeromorphic morphism F : X → Z such that F|S is the given map ϕ followed by that embedding and X \ S ≃ Z \ W, F−1 (|W|) = |S|, |F−1 (w)| = |ϕ−1 (w)| (w ∈ W). (4.14) The natural map OZ → F∗OX is an isomorphism, and the fibers are connected. For a sufficiently divisible global index ℓ of S, the actual line OX(−ℓS) is F-ample; in particular F is projective. More generally an actual rational line on X whose restriction to S is ϕ-ample is F-ample. The target is in Fujiki’s class C.
